title: [claude draft] Tulip mania (1637)
note: Claude draft, not Nandu's final script. Narration is exactly as drafted. Tags are Claude's own tagging, so the score tests the tagging, not the script. Historical facts are not yet checked against sources.
logline: A tulip bulb market booms and crashes, and the lesson is the crowd's certainty, not the flower.
narration: Holland, sixteen thirty-seven. Stories say one tulip bulb costs more than a house. People trade bulb contracts in taverns. A bulb that no one has even dug up yet changes hands again and again. A craftsman earns about three hundred guilders a year. A famous bulb is said to sell for thousands. Everyone thinks the price only goes up. Then, in early February, a bulb auction in Haarlem finds no buyers. Panic spreads. Prices fall. Contracts become paper nobody wants. Now the twist. Historians say the legend is bigger than the truth. Few people were ruined. Records are thin. Still, the lesson sticks. When everyone is sure a price can't fall, ask who is left to buy. That is the real danger of a crowd. Not the flower. The certainty.
